faq_title: Questions we get asked about Bekamak automatic band saws

faq.q: Roller feed or shuttle vise — which is better?
faq.a: Roller feed (BMSO 230–440, BMSO E) is simple and fast for bar and tube in straight cuts; the encoder versions measure the fed length for better accuracy. A servo shuttle vise (BMSO GS/GLS, 270DGS, and all CS/CGS double-column saws) grips the bar and moves it on a ball screw, giving ±0.1 mm repeatability and reliable feeding of bundles and short remnants.

faq.q: How many lengths can I program?
faq.a: The NC control on the servo-feed models stores a job list of several length-and-quantity pairs (and the miter angle on GS/DGS models), so one bar can be cut into different parts without re-programming.

faq.q: What happens at the end of the bar?
faq.a: The saw stops when the remaining length is shorter than the next part or the feed vise reaches its limit, and the counter shows how many pieces were cut. Remnant length depends on the model — typically 3–6 in (80–150 mm).

faq.q: Do automatic saws need a roller table?
faq.a: A short infeed roller table is included on the BMSO E models; a 10 ft (3 m) manual or motorized roller table is optional on the others and is strongly recommended for bars longer than about 6 ft.
